target_customer: Developers and software companies in healthcare, finance and logistics who automate legacy Windows desktop apps for their own clients
problem: Legacy desktop software such as EHRs and ERPs has no good API, so teams use brittle scripts, legacy RPA tools or people clicking and typing.
business_model: Usage-based developer API and SDKs with a Windows driver
product_category: Computer use agent, desktop automation for developers

founders.name: Mahmoud Al-Madi
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built AI and ML solutions at Baylor and Texas Children's, co-published with the Rice Networks Group, and built RPA solutions affecting 20K+ employees at an unnamed Fortune 100 company.

founders.name: Alan
previous_startups: Consumer AI app scaled to thousands of paying users (unnamed)
founders.background_notes: Last name not given on the YC page. Described as having dropped out; the page says the founders met through shared experiences at Rice.

competitors.name: UiPath
competitors.what: Legacy RPA platform for desktop automation

competitors.name: Cua
competitors.what: Open source sandboxes for computer-use agents, compared by commenters

technical_complexity.rationale: A self learning agent that memorizes and replays tasks while adapting to popups and crashes on Windows machines, plus a driver, SDKs and retries, is demanding but built on available vision-language models.

defensibility.rationale: Model providers and RPA vendors can add similar agents; the open source driver and workflow memory add little lock-in beyond integration effort.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Labs and RPA vendors shipped computer-use agents through 2025; no acquisition of Cyberdesk found.

market_need_then: Healthcare and logistics firms rely on legacy Windows apps without APIs and the founders report a customer automating hospital patient intake in production; computer-use models matured in 2024 and 2025.

branding.domain_note: Uses cyberdesk.io. Other companies use the name, including a Munich security firm at cyberdesk.app and older trademark holders.

identity.visual_style: Developer docs style site with HIPAA and SOC 2 badges

branding.community_and_virality: Launch HN post in August 2025 and a Product Hunt listing; no evidence of merch or community.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive compound name shared with other firms and trademark filers, and little brand coverage found.

pivots.from: Open source virtual desktops for building computer agents
pivots.to: Computer use agent for developers to automate legacy Windows apps
pivots.why: Interest came from hobbyists while companies already had VM infrastructure they liked, per the YC launch page as summarized by search; exact date not stated.

outcome_analysis: Cyberdesk is active with two founders in San Francisco. After a pivot from open source virtual desktops to a Windows legacy app agent, it joined YC in Summer 2025 and reports production use in healthcare. No funding is confirmed and labs and RPA vendors are moving into the same space, so the outcome is open.
notes: VC Backed and Caplight list a 500K pre-seed in September 2025 with Y Combinator, aggregator only, so not recorded as a round. A Munich company named CyberDesk (cyberdesk.app) has an unrelated 2026 seed and is excluded. Alan's surname not found. Name origin not found. Completeness pass: the 500K pre seed dated 2025-09 rests on a single database (VCBacked; Caplight also shows 500K total).
